bug_semantics: An authenticated n8n member could preserve attacker-controlled responseText containing script while making the Form node's expression-evaluated respondWith resolve to redirect. renderFormCompletion loaded responseText regardless of the selected response mode, omitted the sandbox Content-Security-Policy whenever respondWith was redirect, and passed both values to a Handlebars completion template that preferred responseText and emitted it with triple braces. A visitor submitting the public form therefore received the attacker's raw HTML without the sandbox and the script executed from the n8n origin with the visitor's session context.
flaw_origin: The mechanism was assembled in two steps. Commit 7ea920dbe742c0ca7c79c9df749aa7d7c898c571 intentionally stopped sanitizing responseText but simultaneously installed an unconditional sandbox CSP, so it did not yet create the advisory's same-origin execution path. Commit 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c then made that CSP conditional on respondWith not being redirect while leaving responseText loaded and rendered independently of respondWith. That guard removal is the smallest commit that completed the vulnerable combination.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names human author Michael Kret <88898367+michael-radency@users.noreply.github.com> and committer GitHub <noreply@github.com>; its message is only 'fix(n8n Form Node): CSP headers should not be set on response with redirect (#20864)' and has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot-author marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-rmr5-775f-jvm2 and its GitHub API record describe the precise redirect/responseText/CSP bypass; the API vulnerability entries give patched ranges >=1.123.69, >=2.34.1, and >=2.33.4, matching the assigned alias bundle. In the validated clone, `git log HEAD -L 117,119:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts` traces the CSP lifecycle: 7ea920dbe742c0ca7c79c9df749aa7d7c898c571 added unconditional SANDBOX_CSP, then 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c changed it to `if (respondWith !== 'redirect')`. `git grep` at the BIC shows formCompletionUtils.ts:58 always loads responseText, :74-76 skips CSP for redirect, and :83 passes responseText; packages/cli/templates/form-trigger-completion.handlebars:108-111 checks responseText first and emits `{{{responseText}}}` before its redirect branch. Direct parent-tree inspection with `git show f527ae125233064c9f6a1293dd5e34e4a1b0a4b7:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Form/utils/formCompletionUtils.ts` shows the raw responseText already present but CSP set unconditionally, proving the completed bypass absent in the immediate parent. `git cat-file -p 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c` establishes sole parent f527ae125233064c9f6a1293dd5e34e4a1b0a4b7 and the human/no-trailer commit object. Tag containment starts at n8n@1.117.0 (and includes n8n@2.0.0); `git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns false for n8n@1.116.2, placing the BIC before the affected lines. Fix carrier 3e4fb19caf73276a68b38d45d96b3da5baf7cab7 changes responseText to be read only when respondWith is showText; its containing 1.x tags start exactly at n8n@1.123.69. Equivalent branch carriers 170cfc787015d352488f6b6403af07a74e95ca1d and 0405fc550f55051f6c459252f5860fa78d27ab80 first occur in n8n@2.34.1 and n8n@2.33.4 respectively. `git log --all -S` for the old unconditional responseText assignment finds only these aggregate bundle carriers (plus identical-tree mainline/private carriers ca3d42d8386515cd9f044377a15a632cd09b62f0 and c4488a956f3d48e53c5aa3cc6a99c5851e8b2009), so no public standalone atomic fix SHA is available and direct_fix_sha is justified null.
reasoning: The advisory's security boundary is origin isolation, not merely the presence of raw HTML. The earlier 7ea920dbe742c0ca7c79c9df749aa7d7c898c571 allowed intentional custom HTML and script but coupled it to an unconditional sandbox CSP; the immediate parent of 7f651ca5a3162ba0f13242dc934047e32998b33c still had that guard. The BIC introduced a mode-dependent CSP exception without coupling responseText to showText. Because n8n parameters can resolve from expressions, respondWith could evaluate to redirect while a saved responseText remained populated; the template then chose and rendered responseText instead of the redirect UI, now without the sandbox. The August 2026 fix closes precisely that data/control mismatch by blanking responseText unless respondWith is showText, and the three backports align exactly with the advisory's patched tag boundaries. The BIC is an ordinary single-parent commit rather than a squash requiring member decomposition. Its commit object provides human authorship and no AI attribution; later bot-authored aggregate fix carriers are irrelevant under the BIC-only attribution rule. The causal and attribution evidence therefore closes as NOT_AI.
